No prior sales data or notes are available yet.", "plan": "Test a mid-range price to gauge demand, then adjust toward the revenue-maximizing point using observed profit each round.", "insight": "Profit per unit equals price minus 3.20, so price should sit well above cost but below the 14.41 ceiling.", "price": 9.50}

{"observations": "Round 1 price 9.50 sold only 0.2 units for profit 1.42. Competitor priced at 4.72, well below us, suggesting strong price competition and that our high price limits volume.", "plan": "Test a lower price nearer the competitor to gain volume, while staying above cost 3.20, then compare profit per round to find the best balance.", "insight": "Units sold at 9.50 were very low, so demand is price-sensitive; profit depends on both margin and volume, and undercutting may raise total profit.", "price": 6.00}

{"observations": "Round 2 at 6.00 sold 33.7 units for 94.28 profit, far above round 1's 9.50 price which sold only 0.2 units. Competitors sit near 4.72-5.75, so we are priced above them.", "plan": "Test a price slightly above the competitor, around 5.90, to keep strong volume while improving margin over cost 3.20, then compare profit per round against the 6.00 result.", "insight": "Demand is highly price-sensitive near competitor levels; volume collapses above roughly 9, so a price just under 6 captures most sales while keeping a healthy per-unit margin.", "price": 5.9}

{"observations": "Round 3 at 5.90 sold 26.5 units for 71.58 profit, below round 2's 6.00 result (33.7 units, 94.28). Competitor prices fell to 5.26, pressuring volume.", "plan": "Price slightly below the competitor's 5.26 drop to recapture volume while keeping margin above the 3.20 unit cost, then compare profit against the round 2 result.", "insight": "Competitor prices are falling and volume responds sharply to small price gaps, so matching or undercutting competitors near 5.2-5.3 likely beats pricing above them.", "price": 5.2}

{"observations": "Round 4 at 5.20 sold 45.4 units for 90.77 profit, beating round 3's 5.90 price. Competitor moved to 5.22, so volume responds strongly to small price gaps near 5.2.", "plan": "Stay just below the competitor's 5.22 to keep volume high, testing a price slightly above cost and comparing profit to round 4's 90.77.", "insight": "Profit peaks where we undercut competitors narrowly; volume gains outweigh the lower margin around 5.1-5.2 given the 3.20 unit cost.", "price": 5.12}

{"observations": "Round 5 at 5.12 sold 40.2 units for 77.23 profit, below round 4's 90.77 at 5.20. Competitor fell to 4.92, undercutting our price, so volume dipped.", "plan": "Test a price slightly above the competitor's 4.92 but below 5.20, around 5.00, to recover margin while staying competitive and comparing profit to round 4.", "insight": "Undercutting a falling competitor further sacrifices margin without guaranteed volume gains; the best profit came at 5.20-5.22, so match near the competitor rather than chasing lower.", "price": 5.00}

{"observations": "Round 6 at 5.00 sold 43.0 units for 77.45 profit, slightly below round 4's 90.77 at 5.20. Competitor fell to 4.89, pressuring margins. Profit per unit peaked near 5.20.", "plan": "Test a price near the competitor's 4.89 but slightly above it, around 4.95, to hold volume while recovering some margin versus 5.00.", "insight": "Profit is driven by margin times volume; dropping price below ~5.00 yields diminishing returns, so stay close to competitors without undercutting aggressively.", "price": 4.95}

{"observations": "Round 7 at 4.95 sold 43.3 units for 75.74 profit, slightly below round 6 at 5.00 (77.45). Competitors have drifted down to about 4.84.
